summary: myidsan gains LDAP/Active Directory login (Phase 1 of docs/MYIDSAN_ENTERPRISE_SSO_PLAN.md), covering AD, Samba AD, FreeIPA, OpenLDAP, and 389-ds. A new pure-Go infra/login/ldap.go performs a service-account bind, a single-entry search from a filter-escaped username template (ambiguous or unmatched results fail closed), then binds as the found user with the supplied password; transport is always TLS (implicit ldaps or StartTLS, optional pinned CA) and an empty/NUL password is refused before any network I/O, closing the classic anonymous-bind bypass. The directory connection is a new DB-backed singleton (DirectoryConfig, apps/myidsan/entities/directory_config.go) configured from a new Federation -> Directory admin page (GET/PUT /api/directory-config, POST /api/directory-config/test which validates the submitted-but-unsaved settings and never binds as a sample user); the bind password is encrypted at rest via infra/atrest, myidsan's first at-rest-encrypted secret. A new FederatedGroupMapping table maps a directory group (matched case-insensitively, highest priority wins) to a myidsan role, resolved on every LDAP login; an Authoritative toggle decides whether the mapping re-applies every login or only seeds a still-pending account once - no match leaves an account's role untouched, so pending-clearance stands. POST /api/login/ldap (SPA) and a new account-type selector on the server-rendered /api/auth/login page (rendered only while directory login is enabled) both authenticate through services.IDirectoryService.AuthenticateLdap, which resolves the account via the existing strict (provider, subject) UpsertFederated dedup shared with Google/GitHub. Separately, this change adds a per-IP failed-login lockout (the same shared LoginGuard mymatasan/myiotsan already use, config block loginSecurity) to myidsan's local login, the new LDAP login, and the federated login page's POST - myidsan previously had no failed-login throttling on any credential surface. A new myidsan_federated_login_total{provider,result} metric counts LDAP outcomes (invalid credential, unreachable, ambiguous, no email, identity conflict, disabled, inactive) so directory failures are visible in aggregate rather than only as individual failed sign-ins.
compatibility: Backward compatible: directory login is off by default (no DirectoryConfig row until an admin saves one and checks Enabled), so existing installs see no change in login behavior until an operator opts in. The account-type selector on both login surfaces is rendered only while directory login is enabled, so local-only deployments see no UI change. The new per-IP login lockout uses the existing shared loginSecurity config block and its documented defaults (5 attempts/300s window, 60s base lockout); state is in-memory and per source IP, resetting on restart, same as the other apps that already use it. Enabling encryption-at-rest for the new bind-password secret follows the existing security.encryptAtRest default (on); a missing key that previously existed fails myidsan's boot closed rather than silently orphaning the encrypted secret. Not yet verified against a real AD/Samba directory - unit-tested (filter escaping/injection, empty-password refusal, objectGUID decode, mapping priority/tie-break, secret roundtrip) and live-booted against a fake host only.
